A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between the appendices and main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original next-token prediction and adaptive world modeling experiments in Sections 3–5, plus appendix experiments on context length, reasoning ablations and topology hints.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental outcomes for open-weights and frontier language models in Sections 3–5 and the appendices, including representation analyses and task accuracy results.

M1.justification: The graph-tracing procedure, adaptive world modeling prompts, representation analyses and model inference procedures remain unchanged. The new conceptual diagram explains the existing framework.

E1.justification: Both versions use 16- and 25-state lines and 4-by-4 and 5-by-5 grids for next-token prediction and adaptive world modeling. The explicit-topology, longer-context, metalearning, reasoning-ablation and hint scenarios already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same Gemma-3, OLMo-2, Gemini-2.5 and GPT-5 variants and the naive adjacency baseline. No evaluated comparator is added, removed or substantively revised.

E3.justification: The reported 1,000-assignment task evaluations, Table 1 context lengths, few-shot example counts and thinking budgets are unchanged. v2 explicitly describes the existing correctness criterion without reporting a changed evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The representation-quality comparison from v1 Appendix A moves into Section 3 and Figure 5. The explicit-grid, relative-Dirichlet-energy, longer-context, metalearning, thinking-ablation and hint analyses are retained; no new analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: The existing error bars and shaded uncertainty bands are retained. There are no changes to run or seed disclosures, uncertainty estimation procedures or statistical testing.

E6.justification: Matched main-text and appendix results are unchanged, including Table 2 accuracies of 53.3%, 52.1%, 33.3% and 31.2%. The redrawn thinking-ablation plots in v2 Figures 18 and 20 preserve the accuracy values in v1 Figures 17 and 19.

T1.justification: The Dirichlet Energy and Distance Correlation definitions in Equations (1)–(3), relative-energy computation and naive-baseline reasoning are unchanged. Moving the deployability definition into a footnote adds no formal content.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central contributions: the adaptive world modeling task, open-weights models' difficulty using learned representations, and frontier reasoning models' limited success. Abstract and introduction edits preserve these claims.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning deployment of topology information and the possible role of reasoning chains remain the same. Section 7 retains the absence of a proposed remedy and uncertainty about reasoning mechanisms; the expanded Section 3 discussion already appeared in v1 Appendix A.

D1.justification: v2 Section 3 explicitly states that a prediction is correct when it belongs to the valid-next-token set given the sequence and topology. This clarifies scoring documentation; the remaining prompt, context-selection and implementation information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 removes Loureiro et al. (2021) and replaces OpenAI Team's 2024 'Learning to reason with LLMs' citation with Jaech et al.'s 'OpenAI o1 System Card.' The broader positioning at the intersection of world models and in-context learning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 streamlines parts of the introduction, standardizes LM terminology, moves the deployability definition into a footnote and incorporates former Appendix A into Section 3. Affiliations and acknowledgments are updated, while the overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds explanatory Figure 1, moves v1 Figure 8 into the main text as Figure 5 with clearer labels, and expands Figure 3's caption. Two appendix plots receive updated titles and plotting presentation; retained figures and tables are reflowed and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new Figure 1 and revised introduction clarify the distinction between encoding representations and using them. Bringing the existing prompt-format control into Section 3, improving figure labels and explicitly documenting correctness make the argument easier to follow and assess. These are modest gains in clarity and documentation; the scientific results and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
